synopsis.heading: Set up the compass first
synopsis.body: Draw North at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right and West on the left before you read the question. Mark the start point with a dot and draw every move as you read it. Most mistakes come from turning in your head.

synopsis.heading: Left and right turns
synopsis.body: A right turn is clockwise and a left turn is anticlockwise, measured from the direction the person is currently facing, not from North. Facing East, a right turn leads South.

synopsis.heading: Shortest distance
synopsis.body: When the path forms a right angle, the shortest distance back to the start is the hypotenuse: √(x² + y²), where x is the net East–West movement and y is the net North–South movement.

formulas.label: Morning sun
formulas.value: Sun in the East, shadow falls West

formulas.label: Evening sun
formulas.value: Sun in the West, shadow falls East

tricks.title: Cancel opposite moves
tricks.body: Add all North moves, subtract all South moves; do the same for East and West. You only need the two net values to find the final position.
tricks.example: 5 N, 3 E, 2 S, 1 W → 3 N and 2 E

tricks.title: Remember the common triples
tricks.body: Exam distances are usually Pythagorean triples. Spot 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 6-8-10 and 8-15-17 and skip the square root.
tricks.example: Net 6 km N and 8 km E → 10 km away

tricks.title: Count right turns
tricks.body: Each right turn adds 90° clockwise; each left turn subtracts 90°. Two rights face the opposite way, four rights face the start direction.
tricks.example: Facing North, R, R, L → East
